data.claim: GitHub publishes no fixed HydraFusion roster, so ddflow cannot ship a default family set: hydrafusion ships as a router with NO members and refuses until the operator fills [agent].routers.
data.falsifier: A GitHub source publishing HydraFusion's complete provider roster would let the default carry members.
data.mechanism: The launch post names only the benchmark models Claude Opus 5 (Anthropic) and GPT-5.6 Sol (OpenAI), and says new Copilot models are incorporated into its model pool. The official announcement (community discussion #206492) says: 'The lineup shifts as new models ship and our evals show what performs best, so we don't publish a fixed roster.' Copilot also serves Gemini (Google) models, so a guessed {anthropic, openai} could wrongly pass a google reviewer as independent. Design: a NEW knob [agent].routers (dict[str, list[str]], model-name substring -> set of families), not list values in [agent].families: families is dict[str,str] with a k=v env notation and is read by reviewer-side code (services/review.py) where a model must have ONE family; widening its value type would make every family_for consumer handle sets. _coerce_dict already supports dict[str, list[str]] (JSON from env), so the knob fits the idiom. Independence for a set author: the reviewer family must be outside the whole set; an empty set is never independent and the refusal names [agent].routers.
data.probe: Fetched the launch post and community discussion #206492; searched for any published HydraFusion roster
data.probe_output: post: models named only as benchmark baselines (Claude Opus 5, GPT-5.6 Sol); pool grows as Copilot adds models. discussion #206492 FAQ: 'We don't publish a fixed roster. The point is that you get the right model without choosing one.' No source lists the providers.
data.question: Which provider families does Copilot HydraFusion route a task across, and how should ddflow model a router author's family set?

data.body: Operator 2026-10-01 asked whether ddflow can work with GitHub Copilot CLI's Project HydraFusion (research R7dbec5e53a, https://github.blog/ai-and-ml/github-copilot/project-hydrafusion-frontier-quality-via-multi-model-orchestration/). It can drive it through the existing copilot target, but: family_for('hydrafusion') == '' so complete refuses ('author's model is not in [agent].families'), and HydraFusion picks models across providers per task (single / cascade / critique), so no single author family exists; its internal different-family critique is invisible to ddflow and is not gate evidence. Scope: (a) [agent].routers (or a families value that is a list): a model name that maps to a SET of families, shipped default hydrafusion -> an EMPTY set: research R-hydrafusion-families (CONFIRMED) found GitHub publishes no fixed roster, so a guessed set could wrongly pass a reviewer as independent; the operator lists the families per plan. Chosen shape: a new knob [agent].routers (dict[str, list[str]]), not list values in [agent].families; (b) reviewer_independence: an author that is a set is independent of a reviewer only if the reviewer's family is outside the WHOLE set; a router author with an unknown member set is never assumed independent -- the refusal names the knob to set; (c) once the set is configured, complete/merge --model hydrafusion works with this repo's DeepSeek reviewer iff deepseek is outside the set; (d) github-copilot delta: HydraFusion is strongest on first-turn single-prompt tasks (per the post), so drive it per step -- claim, then one HydraFusion turn for implement, then ddflow gates -- not the whole loop in one conversation; its internal critique does not replace rubber_duck/critic. Regression tests: hydrafusion author + deepseek reviewer -> independent; + a reviewer in the set -> refused naming the overlap; an unconfigured router -> refused with the knob named; a plain single-family author unchanged. Fails on current code.

Review HIGH "router side not lowercased" refuted: config.router_set returns members stripped+lowercased and test_a_reviewer_inside_the_set_is_refused_naming_the_overlap configures ["Anthropic", ...] and is refused.

family_of/family_for stay the single name->family lookup; router_set is the only reader of [agent].routers (one caller, reviewer_independence); it mirrors family_for case-blind substring matching on purpose but returns a set, and folding it into family_for would make every reviewer-side caller (services/review.py) handle sets; the existing _coerce_dict dict[str,list[str]] path is reused for env parsing, no new parser

titles: ddflow/config.py `router_set` (the `for needle, members in routers.items():` loop)

data.summary: router_set returns the FIRST matching [agent].routers needle, so overlapping needles (hydra + hydrafusion, or hydrafusion + hydrafusion-pro) give an under-approximated or wrong set depending on key order, and a reviewer from an omitted family passes reviewer_independence as independent (false pass). Found by the rubber_duck and critic re-review.

data.rule: When a substring map returns a SET that a safety check compares against, take the union of every matching key (and treat any empty match as unknown); first-match-wins on key order under-approximates the set and turns into a false pass.
data.title: A set-valued lookup must union every match, not stop at the first

evidence.note: Earlier mutation run (all mutants killed) plus the review round: bug B15af2d6420 (router_set first-match under-approximated the family set, a false independent) found by rubber_duck/critic re-review, recorded, failing-first tests committed (3 failed on 1b414fb), fixed in 22ce155 by taking the union of every matching router; final re-review 0 findings on both gates.
